events.headline: Starship Flight 15: the ship is caught from orbit for the first time, but the booster is lost
events.summary: After about 22 hours and 14 orbits, Ship 42 was caught by the Starbase tower arms on Nov. 14, a first for an orbital upper stage, after releasing 26 Starlink satellites. The Super Heavy booster aborted its catch, was diverted toward the Gu…

events.headline: Euclid's first major data release covers more than 900 million galaxies
events.summary: ESA's DR1-Foundation spans about 13 months of observing and 1,900 square degrees, with more than 900 million galaxies, about 15,000 gravitational-lens candidates and over 60 million quasar candidates. It is roughly 14% of the area Euclid w…

events.headline: A young Type Ia supernova in NGC 1433 is one of the nearest since 2011
events.summary: SN 2026ahvu was detected by ATLAS on Nov. 2 and confirmed as Type Ia with Keck II the next day, then imaged by DECam and Gemini South. About 50 million light-years away in NGC 1433, it was caught still brightening and is expected to peak b…

events.headline: A radio-pulsing white dwarf with a Sun-like companion is found 5,000 light-years away
events.summary: GPM J071507−114153 sends a radio signal every eight minutes, matching the spin of a white dwarf that orbits a Sun-like G-type star. The Murchison Widefield Array found it and MeerKAT pinpointed it; the white dwarf's orbital motion was seen…

events.headline: SpaceX targets Nov. 13 for Starship Flight 15, aiming to catch both booster and ship
events.summary: SpaceX released Flight 15 details on Nov. 7: the Super Heavy booster is to be caught minutes after liftoff and the ship about 22.5 hours later, after roughly 14 orbits, pending regulatory approval.

events.headline: Rubin Observatory's early data reveals a new ultra-faint Milky Way satellite and a hidden star cluster
events.summary: Aquarius IV, an ultra-faint satellite galaxy, and Rubin-GC1, a star cluster behind the dusty far side of the Milky Way, both turned up in preview data taken between April 2025 and January 2026, covering about 15% of the survey footprint.

events.headline: ESCAPADE's twin spacecraft complete powered Earth flybys and head for Mars
events.summary: Both NASA ESCAPADE probes used Earth's gravity plus a roughly nine-minute engine burn at closest approach, planned for Nov. 7 and Nov. 9, to speed toward Mars. Each burn was planned to add more than 1,000 mph.

events.headline: A giant hydrogen cloud with no visible stars may be a rotating 'dark' galaxy
events.summary: Swinburne University astronomers, comparing Arecibo and FAST radio surveys, found AGC 322753: about 2 billion solar masses of hydrogen, at least 40 times its stellar mass, with a double-peaked signal that may mean rotation.

events.headline: Webb finds the most distant ring galaxy yet
events.summary: Webb spotted GS18660, a galaxy with a ring of newborn stars, as it was about 2.1 billion years after the Big Bang. A companion moving away at about 425 km/s hints that a smaller galaxy may have punched through its centre.

events.headline: Voyager 1 trims its power use and resumes contact after a brief pause
events.summary: NASA's Voyager team finished swapping three devices for lower-power alternatives in early September. Communications were briefly interrupted around October 18–20 and have been maintained since.

events.headline: NASA asks industry how to boost, service or retire Hubble
events.summary: NASA issued a Request for Information on October 29 seeking industry interest in raising Hubble's orbit, servicing it, or bringing it down in a controlled re-entry. Hubble has sunk by more than 30 km since its last boost in 2009.

events.headline: A rose-colored Sahara rock is one of the oldest Mars meteorites
events.summary: A NASA-funded study in Science reports that Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara in 2022, formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Zircon crystals dated the rock, and it shows signs of alteration by early water.

events.headline: Roman Space Telescope enters science commissioning, 'fully functional'
events.summary: After checkout of the observatory and its main instrument, NASA says Roman can guide, expose and slew between targets, and tests in crowded star fields and dusty nebulae went well.

events.headline: NASA lays out how SpaceX and Blue Origin landers will reach the Moon for 2028 missions
events.summary: SpaceX will aggregate propellant across tanker Starships in orbit, while Blue Origin will skip propellant transfer and use three transfer stages. Landers and Orion will no longer meet in a near-rectilinear halo orbit.

events.headline: NASA ends Swift's science mission after 22 years; uncontrolled re-entry expected within weeks
events.summary: Swift made its final observation on Oct. 20 after atmospheric drag pulled it below 171 miles (275 km), too low to hold steady on targets. A $30 million rescue attempt by Katalyst's LINK spacecraft was called off after control problems.
